title: Crisp Iced Black Tea with Lemon and Mint
summary: Black tea steeps 4 minutes in boiling water, ice water is added to halt the brew, then it is strained, chilled and served over ice with lemon and mint.

ingredients.item: loose black tea, such as Ceylon or Assam

steps.title: Brew
steps.text: Put the tea in the bowl, pour over the boiling water and steep for 4 minutes.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Add the ice-cold water and leave for 1 hour. The cold water stops the brew, so the tea stays bright rather than bitter.

steps.title: Strain and chill
steps.text: Strain into the pitcher and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, until cold.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into ice-filled glasses and finish each with a lemon wedge and a mint sprig. Sweeten at the table if you like.

steps.title: Cold-steep option
steps.text: Instead of brewing hot, steep 8 g tea in 1 litre cold water in the fridge for 5 hours, then strain. It is softer and never clouds.

tips: Cooling too fast in the fridge can make hot-brewed tea cloudy; the ice-water step prevents this.
Ceylon gives a brisk, bright tea; Assam is maltier.
Sweeten with simple syrup rather than sugar, which won't dissolve in cold tea.
Add the lemon at serving; left in the pitcher, the peel turns bitter.
storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
